Lucknow’s Education Map Expands: New Campuses Signal a Rethink of Higher Learning

01 Nov 2026, 06:18 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Education Desk · Source: timesofindia.indiatimes.com

3 min read

Key takeawaysLucknow's higher education landscape is undergoing a significant geographical and conceptual expansion. New academic hubs planned at Sarojini Nagar, Chandrawal, and Kakrabad promise dedicated spaces for agriculture, career-oriented courses, and creative disciplines, signaling a broader rethink of what a university campus can offer.

Overview

Lucknow's higher education landscape is undergoing a significant geographical and conceptual expansion. New academic hubs planned at Sarojini Nagar, Chandrawal, and Kakrabad promise dedicated spaces for agriculture, career-oriented courses, and creative disciplines, signaling a broader rethink of what a university campus can offer.

Lucknow University’s Agricultural Campus Push

Lucknow University (LU) is advancing its proposal for a third campus at Piparsand village in Sarojini Nagar to host agriculture programs. The registrar’s office submitted a land verification report to the UP higher education department, which has forwarded it to the district magistrate’s office for clearance before the final proposal reaches the state cabinet.

  • Confirmed Information: An eight-member committee formed by the sub-divisional magistrate identified agricultural land in July 2024. The registrar’s office submitted the verification report along with Dean of Agriculture Gauri Saxena.
  • Reported Claims: Registrar Bhavana Mishra stated the university visited the site and awaits clearance from the district magistrate’s office. LU Vice-Chancellor Prof JP Saini noted the proposed 50-hectare campus will accommodate the agriculture faculty and expand academic infrastructure.

National PG College’s Career-Oriented Expansion

National PG College is set to expand its footprint with a new campus at Chandrawal on Bijnor Road. The proposal was approved at the governing council meeting, with academic activity expected from the 2027-28 session.

  • Confirmed Information: The campus spans 17 acres allotted by Motilal Memorial Society. Proposed programs include biotechnology, law, agriculture, BBA in agro, food technology, and dairy technology.
  • Reported Claims: Principal Prof Devendra Kumar Singh stated the expansion allows the introduction of "future ready courses" and better facilities, noting construction is underway with an expected completion by July 2027.

Bhatkhande Sanskriti Vishwavidyalaya’s Cultural Vision

The proposed campus at Kakrabad represents a major conceptual shift, envisioned as more than an extension of the existing Kaiserbagh campus. The state has provided approximately six acres, planned around music, dance, theatre, visual arts, filmmaking, literature, and emerging cultural technologies.

  • Confirmed Information: A high-level committee of musicians, dancers, theatre practitioners, and academicians recently discussed a roadmap. The proposed campus includes a school of music and dance, visual and fine arts, film and literature, arts management, a school of theatre, and an AI music lab, alongside grand auditoriums and an innovation zone.
  • Reported Claims: Former director of National School of Drama Vaman Kendre suggested integrating digital arts and virtual production with traditional disciplines. Kathak danseuse Shovana Narayan emphasized the need for the university to remain a "living centre of artistic practice." Malini Awasthi and architecture expert Vandana Sahgal stressed retaining the 'guru-shishya' tradition while building interactive public spaces.

Beyond Lucknow

This expansion is not limited to Lucknow. Indian Institute of Management-Lucknow’s Noida campus (established 2005) and Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University’s Amethi campus (established 2016) demonstrate how institutions have already extended their academic footprint through satellite campuses.

Practical Implications and Verification

These expansions reflect a strategic move to address growing student demand and industry needs across diverse sectors. To verify the original announcements, readers can consult official notices from the UP higher education department regarding LU’s land clearance, the college governing council minutes for National PG College, and official statements from Bhatkhande Sanskriti Vishwavidyalaya regarding the Kakrabad campus roadmap.

Confirmed vs. Reported vs. Unknown

  • Confirmed: LU proposal submitted to UP higher education dept; committee identified land in July 2024; National PG College approved at governing council with 17 acres; Bhatkhande high-level committee discussed roadmap.
  • Reported: Registrar Bhavana Mishra's statement on awaiting clearance; VC Prof JP Saini's statement on 50-hectare campus; Principal Singh's statement on future-ready courses and July 2027 completion; Vaman Kendre's suggestion on digital arts integration; Shovana Narayan's emphasis on artistic practice.
  • Unknown: Exact date of LU's state cabinet approval; exact start date for National PG College academic activity beyond the 2027-28 session; final architectural plans for the Kakrabad campus.
